14.solution:
Take his starting point as the origin, with east and north as the two directions.

North-west is exactly between north and west, so walking 13 m north-west moves him \(\frac{13}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 9.19\) m west and \(9.19\) m north.

Walking 5 m south then brings him back to \(9.19 - 5 = 4.19\) m north of the start, still \(9.19\) m west.

By Pythagoras, his distance from the start is \(\sqrt{9.19^2 + 4.19^2} = \sqrt{84.5 + 17.6} = \sqrt{102.1} \approx 10.1\) m.

So he is about 10.1 m from his initial position.
14.why: Both passes gave 12 m from the 5-12-13 triple, which does not follow from the printed directions; as printed (13 m NW, then 5 m S) he ends about 10.1 m away. Solution rewritten for the printed version (2021 Jun Q27 precedent).
14.notice: The answer usually given is 12 m, from the 5, 12, 13 right triangle, but that does not follow from the directions as printed. Walking 13 m north-west and then 5 m south leaves him about 10.1 m from where he started, which is the answer worked out here.
